12718: Private RV park and marina near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, on 30 acres of private land with abundant walk-on waterfront, run by the McGrady and Brockway families.  Its more than 80 sites run from tent sites to big rigs: fully serviced pull-throughs, full-service 15- or 30-amp sites (some with an ocean view), rustic oceanfront tent sites and The Mecca's four non-serviced group sites.  There is a two-lane launch ramp usable at all tides, a 43-slip marina for boats up to 26 ft, an easy kayak launch and a fish-cleaning station, plus a Level 2 car charger and propane fills up to 100 lb, and Roxy's Diner, a licensed food truck with an ocean-view patio, serves burgers and local lingcod fish and chips.  Partner operators run fishing, bear-viewing and whale-watching tours.  Generators may run from 9 to 11 a.m. and 6 to 8 p.m.  The resort also has long-term RV sites, park-model cottages and two RV trailer rentals, and a residential phase, Orca Views, is coming. --Claude
12737: Newly built campground in a quiet forest setting, nestled against expansive public rainforest in Gibsons on the Sunshine Coast, 5 minutes from the Langdale ferry, beaches and the town centre, with direct access to the Sprockids Mountain Bike Park, Mount Elphinstone and the rainforest trail network.  Most sites have a fire pit, and there are large group sites for events of 100 or more people, and lodges.  Quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude
12739: Campground overlooking Upper Arrow Lake in the heart of the Kootenays, 25 minutes from Nakusp and an hour from Revelstoke; Halcyon Resort's hot-spring pools, spa and dining are 1 km away.  Every site has a lake view except site 4, which looks onto the forest, and sites 23 and 24 are creekside.  Water is at every site, and drinking water and ice are sold at the camp store.  There is a playground, a nature walking trail with cougar and bear exhibits, private waterfalls, a horseshoe pit and cornhole, mountain-bike and e-bike rentals, and backcountry access to biking, ATV and walking trails.  Generators may run at non-electric sites from 9 to 11 a.m. and 4 to 7 p.m., and the person booking must be at least 19.  A lakeview cottage and suite are rented all year. --Claude
12743: Campground beside the St. Mary's River, an 8-minute drive south-west of Kimberley's town centre, the Platzl, with over 150 campsites.  Full-service sites 26-67 and 91-140, in the Mountain View and Pine Meadows areas, take 15- to 50-amp power and rigs of 25 to 45 ft, and the riverview sites 68-79 take 30 or 50 amps and 25 to 35 ft; sites 26, 27, 28, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49, 53-57 and 110-140 are pull-throughs.  The power-and-water back-ins, 1 to 25B (15 or 30 amps, 25 to 40 ft), are closest to the pool and mini-golf, and the non-service sites NS1 to NS9 (20 to 25 ft) are first come, first served.  A free heated pool is open from mid-May to the September long weekend and an 18-hole putting course from early May to late September, and there is a timber picnic shelter, a playground, bocce, horseshoes and sand volleyball.  The Adventure Centre rents e-bikes, stand-up paddleboards and inflatable kayaks and sells Kootenay Rafting Company tours.  Cell service is spotty.  In winter the bathrooms behind the office stay open with running water and hot showers, tanks are filled there from a hose, and the sani-dump is at site 26.  Winter storage costs C$250 from October 1 to April 20.  The campground also rents trailers and trapper's tents and has walk-in tent sites. --Claude
12760: Campground in Metro Vancouver's Brae Island Regional Park, beside the Fraser River at Fort Langley and within walking distance of the historic village; Pathfinder Camp Resorts runs it under licence from Metro Vancouver.  All of its RV sites have 30-amp power and water, and some have 30/50-amp full hookups for self-contained RVs; there is also a group tent area for 65 people (up to 100) and five tent cabins.  The camp store and BERG bike rentals open from Canada Day to Labour Day, propane is sold, and summer weekends are themed.  The campground is gated around the clock, with gate entry cards; showers cost C$2 for 10 minutes, and mosquitoes can be a nuisance when the river runs high. --Claude
12762: Oak Bay Marine Group resort and marina on Pedder Bay, 40 minutes from downtown Victoria, against a backdrop of the Olympic Mountain Range and the Race Rocks Ecological Reserve.  Its fully serviced RV sites are oceanfront, back-in or pull-through, with 30-amp, double 30-amp or 50-amp power, and a seasonal dry-camping area opens from spring to fall, where generators may run from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.  The marina has a fuel dock, a boat-launch ramp, moorage for vessels of 18 to 56 ft, boat and kayak rentals and guided fishing charters.  There is a coffee house and licensed snack bar, an off-leash dog park, and bunkies to rent. --Claude
12768: Resort and marina near Campbell River on the Georgia Strait.  Its Front Row big-rig sites, 16 to 30 ft wide and 60 to 80 ft deep under Douglas firs, overlook the marina, the Georgia Strait and the Coast Mountain Range, and at peak times they need a rig of 25 to 30 ft or more.  Rows A and B, under the trees, are 38 to 45 ft deep; the Main Park has treed sites about 18 ft wide and 46 ft deep, and sunny ones.  The Lighthouse beachfront sites have no trees and a fire pit on a raised seaside berm, and the Lighthouse non-beachfront sites have 50-amp power, many backing onto a nature conservation area.  A heated pool and a hot tub (16 and over) open from mid-May to mid-September; there is an adult rec hall and clubhouse with a stone fireplace, beach volleyball, horseshoes, shuffleboard and swing golf, a seasonal Sugar Shack, a community fire pit and the Oyster River nature trail.  The boat ramp costs C$15 a launch, and there is moorage.  Cottages and park models are also rented. --Claude
12775: Resort across from the Spahats Falls day-use area at the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park, between Kamloops and Jasper, near the Trophy Mountain flower meadows and Helmcken Falls.  It has private forested sites and easy pull-in, pull-out sites, serviced (30-amp power, water and internet) or unserviced, plus group sites, and commercial and work-camp sites with a full-size gymnasium and a helicopter landing area.  There is an outdoor dish sink, sites have picnic tables and fire pits, and firewood is sold.  For swimming, the resort recommends Dutch Lake, 15 minutes away.  Three 1,700 sq ft four-bedroom cottages are also rented, and the minimum stay varies by site type and season. --Claude
12800: RV park in Drumheller, in the Badlands, a short walk from the World's Largest Dinosaur, swimming and downtown, a short drive from the Royal Tyrrell Museum and 15 minutes from the Hoodoos and the Atlas Coal Mine.  Its sites are split between the East Park and the West Park, and portable fire pits are available; there is also an ATM, e-bike rental (C$75 a full day) and four lodgings, from Littlefoot Lodge to the Cabana. --Claude
12805: Campground seconds from Horseshoe Canyon's views and hiking trails and minutes from Drumheller's attractions, with big-rig-friendly sites.  There is a playground, mini-golf, ice cream, fire pits and firewood, and deluxe and camping cabins are rented. --Claude
12812: Daily-fee RV park in Sandy Point, a gated resort community of 800 acres with 4.5 km of natural lakefront on the south-western shore of Gull Lake, 10 minutes west of Highway 2 and 5 km from Bentley; it sits alongside seasonal sites and ownership lots.  Its easy back-in sites are about 100 ft long and 30 ft wide on large gravel pads, each with a view of Gull Lake, a few steps from the public beach.  The resort has an inland marina and boat launch, walking trails and a golf course opening in 2026, and pets are allowed in designated areas only. --Claude
12857: Beach campground minutes from the Confederation Bridge, a stop for those going to or coming from Prince Edward Island.  Its no-service sites are right on the water, steps from the beach, and its 3-way service sites a short walk away.  The on-site store sells groceries, household items, camping essentials, coffee and ice cream, and the beach access, public washrooms and showers serve visitors and campers through the season.  Seasonal sites have a waitlist.  The campground's signature fundraiser, the Cape Tormentine Beach Music Festival, runs from July 30 to August 2, 2026. --Claude
12863: Campground 19 km (12 miles) east of Shediac off Highway 133, at the border of Cap-Pelé and Grand-Barachois, beside Gagnon Beach, with its sunsets, sandbars for miles and what the campground calls the warmest waters north of Virginia.  Every site is 2 to 5 minutes' walk from the sand.  There is an animal-friendly area, a playground with a bouncy pillow, a basketball court, a recreation hall for pool, ping-pong and other indoor games, a new family inground pool and a large field.  Sites run from unserviced field camping to 2-service sites in the main area (20 amps) or the open field (20 or 30 amps) and 3-service sites (30 amps), mostly drive-through.  Wi-Fi costs extra, C$7 a day per device.  The campground also rents trailers and a studio cottage, and seasonal sites have a waitlist.  Max Michaud, Pat Jacob and Fred Jacob have owned it since August 2024; it is over 40 years old.  A beach day pass or visitor pass costs C$10 a carload. --Claude
12872: Campground beside the Mactaquac head pond, part of the Saint John River, across from Nackawic and the World's Largest Axe.  It has a sandy beach and docks for boating and fishing, kayak rentals, a playground, horseshoes and washer toss, and live music, barbecues and pig roasts on summer Saturdays.  Nackawic, 3 minutes away, has groceries, a liquor store, a pharmacy and a marina with a paved launch and fuel; golf is within 5 minutes, and ATV trails and Kings Landing are nearby.  Cabins and trailers are also rented.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m., and a site holds at most 10 people. --Claude
12890: Boutique-style campground overlooking the Saint John River at Hawkshaw, with optional valet parking, an adults-only section and big-rig-friendly sites.  A heated 20 x 40 ft pool, open from the May long weekend to the end of September, has poolside tiki huts and a palapa; there are lawn games, a 64-ft dock for swimming, fishing and boats, kayak and bicycle rentals, a community rec centre, a stage for special events, Level 2 EV chargers (paid) and a book and DVD exchange.  A site holds at most 6 people; day visitors pay C$5 and overnight guests C$8. --Claude
12905: Cottage and campground village on the outskirts of Inverness, above the sandy shores of the Gulf of St. Lawrence between two world-class golf courses, with private beach access, ocean sunsets and the Cabot Trail at its back door; the MacLeod family has run it since 1985.  Its unserviced sites take tents, pop-ups, teardrops, truck campers and small camper vans (18 ft), but no motor homes, RVs or travel trailers, and a site can be locked.  Tents aren't allowed on RV sites.  Wi-Fi is in the cottages but not on the campsites, and ATV stays need the village's approval, 4 at most at a time.  It also has 41 housekeeping cottages. --Claude
12918: William and Sandra Robinson's campground, nestled in the trees across from Hunts Point Beach, a 4-minute walk away; Summerville Beach is an 8-minute drive, Carters Beach 5 minutes past it, and Liverpool 12 km.  Sites are gravel, with a picnic table and fire pit, and two solar-powered sites suit pop-up trailers, vans or tents; three unserviced tent sites have 12 x 12 ft sand pads, and T1 also fits a car or van.  Four rental RVs, 26 to 32 ft, are on site, and so is the Cove Coffee & Snack Bar; e-bikes, hoverboards and propane fire pits are rented.  The shower house is heated, there is a kitchen area, and fresh eggs and live lobsters are sold. --Claude
12925: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites beside the water.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude
12942: Campground at Spencer's Island on the Bay of Fundy, where every site has a front-row seat to the bay.  The land was a shipyard with a lighthouse, then a lumber yard; Bob and Noreen ran the campground from 1999, and Bill and Joanne have since 2023.  Lobster season runs to the end of July, a public boat ramp is right next to the campground, and there is a book exchange.  From June 27 to August 29 the cottages rent by the week only, Saturday to Saturday.  Check Cumberland County's burn restrictions before lighting a fire. --Claude
13124: Small campground in the Appalachian Mountains of Garrett County, family-owned since 1964 (Grace and Doc Shunk), 2 miles from New Germany State Park.  Its rustic, shady sites are mostly back-ins on gravel, with some pull-throughs, and may need levelling; an RV water-filling station and a wash sink stand outside the renovated, heated bathhouse.  The sewer disposal area doesn't accommodate modern RVs but takes a rolling portable tank, and New Germany State Park's dump station is less than 5 miles away.  The small Glamp Store is open around the clock, fiber Wi-Fi arrived in summer 2026, and cell service is limited.  A-frame and other cabins are rented, a new pavilion is coming, and political flags aren't allowed.  CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (a US Census rooftop match on the operator's published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west and Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west), and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop.  Not to be confused with New Germany State Park Campground (id 63), the separate state-run campground nearby. --Claude
13146: Campground among ponderosa pines and rolling hills on SD-79 at Hermosa, a base for Mount Rushmore, Crazy Horse and Deadwood.  It has spacious sites, a dog park, a fire pit and propane; Dollar General and the Lazy R are within walking distance, and Corner Pantry is half a mile away.  Monthly stays are offered at a discounted rate from November 1 to April 1. --Claude
14202: Family campground opened in August 1969 in a gravel pit dug for the highway, and run by three generations of the Riemersma family.  It has a fishing pond with boat rentals, a pool (added in 1975), a rec room, an activity field, a playground and PumpkinFest, and rents cabins.  Rustic pop-up sites take stays of a week at most, holidays and Tulip Time take a 3-night minimum, and clubs are welcome. --Claude
14204: Country campground in Ogemaw County beside a big pond stocked for catch-and-release fishing, with a swimming beach and kayaks, a canoe and paddle boats.  There is volleyball, a playground, a sharing library, basketball hoops and a community area by the pond.  Campers can ride from the campground to the ORV and snowmobile trails, and DNR ORV licences are sold.  It rents tents, sleeping bags, a 2019 VLite camper and cabins.  Clear Lake's public boat launch is a mile away, Ogemaw Nature Park just over 2 miles, and the Rifle River Recreation Area is nearby.  Storage costs $35 a month; electric-only sites can have their fresh-water tanks filled, or their holding tanks emptied by the honey wagon, for a fee, and propane is sold.  Holiday weekends take a 3-night minimum, and a site may have two dogs at most. --Claude
14210: Campground near Boyne Falls with a heated pool, two playgrounds and an 8-acre youth ATV park for riders 16 and younger.  There are yurts, community bonfires, a propane fill station and gasoline, a basketball court, sand volleyball and horseshoe pits, a dog park, a half-mile walking trail, a sunset lookout, a pavilion for event rentals and a zip line for children, and seasonal sites are offered. --Claude
14211: Campground across the road from Lake Huron and near Harrisville State Park, with easy access to the beach; formerly CampDoYaWanna Campground & Party Store, it is now family-owned under new ownership.  Select sites are big-rig friendly, and there are shaded sites, a honey wagon, a car wash, crafts, a playground, gaga ball, sand volleyball, horseshoes and cornhole, and three RV rentals. --Claude
